findings.text: the no-git-process claim is an absence with no positive control on its instrument: assert not calls.exists() passes whether the pass called git or the shim was never reachable, and no line in the case shows the shim recording a call it should see (for example by invoking `git --version` through the same PATH before the assertions). The case's own comment calls the removals the control, but the removals only show the pass completed, not that the shim is on the recording path; the declared mutation's failure of this case is on the removal assertion, not on the shim. A second PATH shim earlier on PATH would also be matched by the same defect.
